---
title: "Read a CSV file into a typed table"
---

Read hourly weather at the three New York City airports in 2013, from
nycflights13's `weather` table in the
[PHPstats datasets](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#weather), straight
from its URL. One column's type is declared, and the rest are guessed:

{{< include _read-a-csv.md >}}

- The 26,115 rows give 16 columns. `rownames` holds the row names the table
  had in R.
- Whole numbers, such as `year`, `hour`, and `wind_dir`, become int, where
  readr's `read_csv()` gives double. Decimals become double.
- `time_hour` holds ISO 8601 text such as `2013-01-01T06:00:00Z`, which is
  guessed as a datetime in UTC.
- `types` declares `origin` a factor, with the levels EWR, JFK, and LGA in
  sorted order. Without it, `origin` would be a string.
- Empty fields become NA: one hour has no temperature, 20,778 of 26,115 have
  no wind gust, and 2,729 have no pressure.
- Types are guessed from up to 1,000 sampled rows. Declare a type when those
  rows could mislead the guess.

Runnable script: [read-a-csv.php](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phibble/main/docs/examples/read-a-csv.php).
It reads the file over HTTPS, so `allow_url_fopen` must be on.

Reference: [Reading and writing data](../io.qmd) · [Types](../types.qmd).
